text:
Evening, Burlington. We're clear and a mild 52 as the sun heads down, with sunset right around 4:23, so catch it if you're out for a walk. It's a pretty one, with a clear sky and an easy breeze. Once the sun's gone the temperature drops quickly, but it won't get frosty. Clouds drift in overnight and hold us to a low around 38, a good 5 to 10 degrees milder than a typical mid-November night. A light jacket will do for the evening.

Tomorrow looks a lot like today: dry, partly sunny, and a high near 55. The NWS forecast has temperatures easing back to around 49 later in the afternoon, so don't leave the house in just a T-shirt. The models agree on mid-50s, though NBC5 is a little more optimistic, with upper 50s possible. Wednesday night is partly cloudy with a low near 37.

Pleasant, dry weather holds through the end of the week. The pattern turns more active early next week, when a cold front looks set to end the warmth.

AFD KEY MESSAGES (forecaster's reasoning, issued 2026-11-17T19:02:00+00:00 — covers the whole BTV area, northern NY included: translate to what Burlington feels, never repeat other regions' place names):
  1. Dry weather with above normal temperatures continues through the end of the week.
  2. The weekend will be unseasonably warm and primarily dry. By Sunday evening, chances for rain increase associated with a possible east coast storm. Then a strong front will bring much colder conditions to the region later Monday into Tuesday.
AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 201 PM EST Tuesday... No significant changes were made with this forecast package.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: A large area of high pressure will maintain generally quiet weather across the area through the end of the work week. Temperatures will run 5-10 degrees above normal through Friday. Highs will generally range through the 50s and lows will range through the 30s into low 40s. The center of the surface high will remain to our south, which will maintain a pressure gradient over our area that will support some light west to southwest winds at the surface, with occasional gusts to around 15 mph possible each afternoon. Higher elevations, especially over northern NY, will see higher gusts. Gusts over the northern Adirondacks will generally be in the 15 to 25 mph range, though higher summits will see gusts in excess of 40 mph at times. These breezes, along with some overnight cloud cover as shortwaves move through, will prevent ideal radiational cooling conditions and will keep lows seasonably mild. KEY MESSAGE 2: Dry conditions are near certain to continue through Sunday morning, with near record daily high temperatures anticipated at long term climate sites. Sunday will mark six consecutive warm days across the region. Thereafter, increasing chances of rain, especially beginning Sunday evening into Monday, will be tied to two systems that will generally converge towards our region. Through early next week, while the risk of impactful weather is low, a more active pattern will begin regardless of how things play out. There are generally three scenarios that model solutions fall into for this period; a mainly dry one, a light rain event with perhaps some higher terrain snow showers in the wake of a cold front, or a moderate rainfall favored in southern/eastern portions of the region. This latter, more noteworthy outcome would occur if low pressure developing later this week forms farther west than the consensus across Florida, which leads to a track hugging the east coast rather than out to sea. The latest run of the GEFS strongly favors an out to sea scenario, but its operational run and many members of the ECMWF EPS and AIFS systems still show a risk of this wetter scenario. The most likely outcome is in the official forecast, which shows some rain showers associated with an incoming cold front from the west that will put an end to our unseasonable warmth. The character of this front is hard to pin down right now; a sharper front could induce some relatively heavy showers and a changeover to snow by Tuesday morning. Otherwise, would expect no impacts with precipitation amounts under 0.25" and more likely under 0.1" in most locations. The final scenario is almost entirely dry with both a miss in the coastal storm and a cold front that produces little precipitation as low pressure weakens to our north as it passes through Monday.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - Our stretch of pleasant November weather continues across Vermont and the North Country, with dry conditions and temperatures running well above normal through the weekend. This stretch of warmth is setting up to even become unprecedented. Not necessarily in the intensity of the warmth, but the duration. Highs will generally reach the 50s, with plenty of sunshine at times. A few showers are possible Sunday night into Monday before a cold front brings a return to much colder weather by Tuesday. Low 36°. Skies will be partly cloudy tonight, with a light west to southwest breeze. Saturday will bring sunshine and a high of 57°, followed by a partly cloudy night with a low of 46°. Sunday will be partly sunny with a high of 56°, and a few showers will be possible Sunday night as temperatures fall to 44°. There’s a chance of showers again Monday, with a high of 48°. The track of a possible coastal system remains uncertain, but a cold front is expected to bring colder air into the region. Monday night’s low will drop to 27°, and Tuesday will be mostly sunny with a high of 36°.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-11-17T18:49:00Z — same caveat): Warming up, with mostly sunny skies Tuesday afternoon — The warmup begins Tuesday afternoon, as highs reach the low to mid-50s. Expect a partly to mostly sunny sky, with a noticeable south breeze. Tonight won't be as cold, with lows in the 30s to around 40, along with a few passing clouds. The Wednesday through Friday stretch looks beautiful, with plenty of sunshine and highs in the upper 50s to low 60s! The nice stretch continues this weekend, as it stays mostly dry and mild. Expect nearly full sunshine Saturday. A south breeze picks up on Sunday, as a cold front approaches. A few late-day showers are likely. Highs will be near 60 both days. Behind the front, more seasonable air returns early Thanksgiving week. Highs fall back to the 30s and 40s. More clouds and a few showers are possible around the holiday, as it turns a bit milder.
